research.summary: The macro backdrop is supportive: the Fed cut rates another 25bp on 2025-12-10 to a 3.50-3.75% target range, the only major event in the curated 60-day feed. On the first trading day of 2026 (Jan 2), the Dow rose 0.7% while the Nasdaq was flat as energy, materials and utilities led and mega-cap tech lagged, with Microsoft down 2.2% on AI-competition concerns. The reference momentum names have strong news support — GE Aerospace near a buy point after an ~84% 2025 climb with defense/aerospace strength expected to persist, and Caterpillar leading the Dow on AI power/data-center demand with a record $39.9B backlog — while GOOGL carries strong price momentum but faces explicit valuation and AI-capex criticism. Near-term risks include overbought readings (GE RSI 74.7, LLY 77.4), Q4 earnings previews flagging earnings declines for CAT and XOM, and LLY/NVO cutting obesity drug prices in China.

forecaster.method_notes: Forecasts are statistical drift-based estimates over the actual 5-trading-day holding horizon (2026-01-02 to next decision 2026-01-09), using only price history up to the decision date; p10/p90 define an 80% interval. SPY is included as the benchmark (expected +0.32%); all expected returns should be judged relative to it, not zero. Largest positive expected excess vs SPY: GE (+1.05pp), CAT (+0.67pp), GOOGL (+0.69pp), GLD (+0.67pp), JNJ (+0.43pp), NVDA (+0.42pp), JPM (+0.39pp), LLY (+0.36pp). Most negative excess: PG (-0.61pp), HD (-0.52pp), SHW (-0.42pp), AMT (-0.34pp), AMZN (-0.27pp), TLT (-0.28pp), LIN (-0.26pp). Limitations: (1) 5-day expected returns are tiny relative to interval widths (e.g., NVDA +0.74% expected vs -7.84/+10.12 band), so wide intervals reflect genuine uncertainty, not avoidability; (2) short-horizon drift estimates are noisy and momentum can mean-revert over days; (3) the model uses price history only and does not incorporate fundamentals, earnings events, or macro news; (4) with 10bps transaction costs each way, round-trip costs (~20bps) are material against single-digit-bpp expected excess returns, favoring concentration in the highest-excess names rather than broad repositioning; (5) confidence scores are signal-to-noise scaled and are uniformly modest given the short horizon.

decision.rationale: I keep the momentum core but trim GE to 0.22 (RSI 74.7 with 30% vol into a 5-day window is the critic's chief mean-reversion flag, though its multi-horizon strength keeps it a top weight) and GOOGL to 0.18 (the only affirmatively negative ticker-specific news in the feed, plus flat 30d momentum and mega-cap tech rotation pressure), while holding CAT near reference since RSI 40.1 shows cooled momentum and the Q4 earnings risk likely sits outside this window. I size GLD at 0.20 — the book's highest forecast confidence (0.58), up on every horizon, and the diversifier the pipeline identified but never sized — and JNJ at 0.15 for a low-vol uptrend with +0.43pp expected excess. Weighted forecast is ~+1.04% gross (~+0.94% net of 10bps entry cost) vs SPY +0.32%, so I stay fully invested with no cash, expecting the portfolio to rise over the window.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-01-09 to next decision 2026-01-16), using only price history up to the decision date; no post-date information. Benchmark is SPY at +0.30% expected over 5 days, so relative value should be judged on excess_return_vs_benchmark, not on sign vs zero: GE (+0.93%), CAT (+0.74%), GLD (+0.74%), GOOGL (+0.71%), JNJ (+0.42%), JPM (+0.34%) screen strongest vs SPY; AAPL (-0.29%), PG (-0.60%), AMT (-0.39%), HD (-0.36%) screen weakest. p10-p90 intervals are wide (roughly +/-3-9%) because they scale with recent 30d volatility over a short horizon; wide intervals are uncertainty about magnitude, not evidence to avoid an asset. Confidence encodes signal-to-uncertainty (expected excess return vs interval width), not probability of profit; all point estimates are small relative to noise, so no forecast is high conviction. Limitations: (1) drift extrapolation captures momentum continuation but not mean reversion, which is a live risk for extended names (GOOGL RSI 88.6, LIN 85.2, AMZN 80.6, SPY 74.0) and a potential bounce tailwind for oversold names (AAPL RSI 21.8); (2) no fundamentals, earnings, macro, or news inputs; (3) 5-day expected returns are noisy and vol estimates can shift abruptly; (4) single-model point estimates, no ensemble; (5) transaction costs (10 bps each way) can exceed the expected excess return of marginal trades over this short window.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 4-trading-day holding horizon (2026-01-16 to 2026-01-23), using only price history up to the decision date; one forecast_universe call supplied all tickers. Expected returns should be compared against the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.26%), not zero: largest positive excess vs SPY are GE (+0.74%), CAT (+0.66%), GLD (+0.59%), GOOGL (+0.59%), JNJ (+0.43%); most negative are PG (-0.43%), HD (-0.26%), META (-0.22%), AMT (-0.20%). Confidence is the approximate probability the direction call is correct, derived from a normal approximation to the p10/p90 band; all confidences are modest (0.49-0.63) because the 4-day horizon is noise-dominated. Limitations: (1) p10-p90 intervals span roughly 4-16 percentage points, far wider than any expected return, so wide intervals reflect genuine uncertainty, not proof an asset should be avoided; (2) the model is purely quantitative price statistics and ignores fundamentals, news, and scheduled events; (3) it assumes drift/momentum persistence and does not capture short-term mean reversion, which is a risk for oversold names (AAPL RSI 10.6, V 24.7, MSFT 26.5, META 29.2) and overbought names (HD 78.5, SHW 76.8, WMT 75.3, CVX 73.6, CAT 73.5, GOOGL 74.3); (4) with 10 bps transaction costs each way, expected excesses under ~0.5% vs SPY may not survive round-trip trading costs; (5) SPY is included for benchmark comparison only and is not tradable in this scenario.

research.summary: The portfolio's core faces a split picture: gold is at record highs near $5,000/oz with banks calling the rally structural, but GLD's RSI of 88.2 flags extreme overbought conditions ahead of the approaching January FOMC. JNJ delivered a Q4 beat ($24.6B sales) with ~$100B 2026 guidance and a TD Cowen target raise to $250, while GE Aerospace's earnings 'worried the market' despite UBS/Citi target hikes and a 74% Q4 order surge. CAT slipped with the Dow on Jan 23 amid Trump Greenland policy whipsaw, and GOOGL retains strong momentum despite a Waymo NTSB probe. The 5-day horizon spans a Big Tech earnings wave (MSFT, META, AAPL, TSLA) and the January FOMC, raising benchmark event risk.

forecaster.method_notes: Forecasts are statistical drift-model estimates over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-01-23 to 2026-01-30), using only price history up to the decision date; SPY is included as the benchmark for comparison. Expected returns should be judged against the SPY forecast (+0.35%), not zero: the largest projected excesses are GLD (+0.84%), CAT (+0.81%), GOOGL (+0.70%), GE (+0.70%), and JNJ (+0.56%), while most other names show small negative excesses. Fundamentals news is otherwise constructive for core holdings: CAT beat Q4 expectations with multiple price-target raises (JPM to $765, Oppenheimer to $729), JNJ hit record highs on strong 2025 results and 2026 guidance plus a talc fraud-lawsuit dismissal, and LLY announced a $3.5B Pennsylvania facility though the EMA declined its Mounjaro heart-failure label. Key binary risk within the 5-day horizon: GOOGL, AMZN, and LLY all report earnings next week, following Microsoft's disappointing results that sent software stocks tumbling. Several holdings and candidates (JNJ RSI 92.7, XOM 91.1, NEE 93.1, PG 75.0) screen as extremely overbought, raising mean-reversion risk over a short horizon.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-01-30 to next decision 2026-02-06), using only data through the decision date; p10/p90 from historical volatility scaling. Benchmark SPY expected +0.31% (p10 -3.07, p90 +3.80); all returns should be judged as excess vs SPY, not vs zero. Largest positive excess vs benchmark: GLD +0.81, GOOGL +0.76, CAT +0.76, GE +0.71, JNJ +0.59, LLY +0.40, NVDA +0.33; current holdings (CAT, GE, GLD, GOOGL, JNJ, LLY) all carry non-negative expected excess, so the forecast supports the existing core. Limitations: (1) 5-day returns are noise-dominated - every expected excess is small relative to its p10-p90 interval, so these are tilts, not certainties; wide intervals reflect uncertainty, not a reason to avoid an asset. (2) The drift method extrapolates recent trend and does not model mean reversion after overbought conditions (XOM RSI 91, CVX 89, NEE 93, JNJ 93, PG 75) or oversold bounces (V 23.5, JPM 29.6, MSFT 31.9), which could flip short-horizon signs. (3) Event/gap risk (e.g., GE's Jan-22 earnings gap, upcoming earnings within the window) is not captured. (4) No news or fundamental integration; confidence values are signal-to-noise scaled and modest by construction. (5) With 10 bps each-way transaction costs (~0.20% round trip), most single-name expected excesses do not justify turnover on forecast alone - favor retaining positions unless a holding's forecast turns clearly negative vs benchmark.

decision.rationale: I cut GLD from 23.5% to 6% and exit GE entirely: the critic verified GLD's -10.3% same-day crash on the hawkish Warsh nomination (a regime shock the drift forecast ignores) and GE's Jan 22 -7.4% gap plus a second negative Q4 verdict, so both reference-allocation legs fail on fresh evidence rather than stale 12-1m momentum. I keep GOOGL (18%) and CAT (20%) as the core on multi-horizon relative strength and CAT's fresh beat with target raises, add WMT (13%) and NVDA (9%) for steady low-vol and repaired-chart momentum, and trim JNJ to 7% for RSI 92.7 mean-reversion risk while holding LLY small (4%) into its binary print. The 23% cash is deliberate event-risk insurance: GOOGL and LLY both report inside the 5-day window (MSFT's -10% gap is the live downside scenario) and the RSI 75-93 overbought cluster leaves no compelling deployment home, so I accept modest benchmark drag rather than force exposure.

research.summary: The week ending Feb 6, 2026 saw a violent AI-driven tech repricing (MSFT's Jan 28 earnings sparked a ~$1T selloff, AMZN fell ~9% on a $200B capex plan) followed by a powerful Feb 6 rebound that pushed the Dow above 50,000 for the first time, led by NVDA (+7.8% after Jensen Huang defended $660B of AI infrastructure spending) and CAT (record high on Q4 revenue of $19.1B and 2026 guidance at the top of its 5-7% CAGR target). Rotation into value, energy, and staples continued: XOM, JNJ (all-time highs, RBC PT raise to $255), and WMT ($1T market cap) are all strong, though many are technically overbought (JNJ RSI 95, XOM 84, PG 84, WMT 77). Gold rebounded after its late-January crash with commentators citing no fundamental breakdown, while the Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% in January after a Dec 10 cut. Over the 5-day horizon, the main tension is between AI-capex sentiment risk (MSFT, AMZN, NVDA, GOOGL) and mean-reversion risk in extended value/defensive names.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift model over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-02-06 to 2026-02-13), using only price history up to the decision date; one forecast_universe call supplied all tickers. Expected returns should be judged against the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.30% expected, p10 -3.09%, p90 +3.80%), not against zero: the largest positive excess-vs-benchmark forecasts are CAT (+0.91pp), GLD (+0.84pp), GE (+0.68pp), JNJ (+0.63pp), GOOGL (+0.72pp) and NVDA (+0.57pp); AMZN, MSFT, HD, AMT and META screen slightly below benchmark. Confidence is a signal-to-noise score (excess return vs benchmark scaled by the p10-p90 half-width), so all calls are low-to-moderate conviction: over 5 days the 80% intervals (roughly +/-3-8%) dwarf the expected drift, and 'flat' vs 'up' labels reflect sub-1% expected moves. Key limitations: (1) the drift model extrapolates recent trends and ignores regime shocks and news - e.g. it would have missed GLD's -10.3% same-day crash on the hawkish Warsh nomination noted in the prior decision, and it cannot see earnings or macro events inside the window; (2) several names are extended (RSI 76-95 for WMT, PG, JNJ, XOM, CVX, NEE, AAPL), creating mean-reversion risk the drift term may over-ride; (3) MSFT, AMZN and AMT show persistent downtrends (below 200-day SMAs) where drift estimates are unstable; (4) 30-day volatility inputs may understate or overstate true 5-day risk if vol is regime-shifting. Wide intervals are uncertainty, not evidence to avoid an asset; relative expected-return ranking vs SPY is the actionable signal.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts from a single forecast_universe call, using only price history through the 2026-02-13 decision date, horizon = 4 trading days (to 2026-02-20). Benchmark SPY: expected +0.22% (p10 -2.81, p90 +3.35); all returns should be judged as excess vs SPY, not vs zero. Largest positive excess vs benchmark: CAT +0.98%, GLD +0.67%, JNJ +0.56%, NVDA +0.48%, GE +0.46%, GOOGL +0.43%, XOM +0.35%; most negative: AMZN -0.49%, META -0.35%, V -0.35%, PG -0.26%, MSFT/HD -0.25%. Confidence = approximate probability of the stated direction under a normal fit to the tool's p10/p90 quantiles (sigma=(p90-p10)/2.56); 'flat' means no directional edge and is assigned 0.50. Limitations: (1) over a 4-day window expected drift (<1.3%) is small relative to p10-p90 spans of roughly 4-14%, so every call is low-conviction and wide intervals reflect volatility/uncertainty, not a signal to avoid an asset; (2) drift models have weak predictive power at short horizons and assume roughly log-normal returns without jumps - earnings, macro data, or positioning reversals inside the window would dominate; (3) no news, fundamentals, or event-calendar information is incorporated; (4) the drift method may understate mean-reversion risk in extended names (JNJ RSI 89, NEE 80.8, CAT 79.8, WMT 78.1, PG 75.6) and bounce potential in deeply oversold names (AMZN RSI 15.9, GOOGL 23.0, MSFT 26.0); (5) most excess-vs-benchmark edges (0.1-0.4%) are modest against 20 bps round-trip transaction costs, so only the top excess names (CAT, GLD, JNJ, NVDA, GE, GOOGL) clear costs with meaningful room.

research.summary: The week ended with the Supreme Court striking down most Trump tariffs (S&P 500 +0.7% Friday, ad/e-commerce/industrial names rallying), but Trump immediately announced new 10% global tariffs, keeping policy risk alive. Stagflation fears intensified as Q4 GDP slowed to 1.4% while core PCE rose to 3%, driving gold back above $5,000/oz and lifting 10-year yields, while Trump's Iran strike threats pushed oil near six-month highs. Nvidia's earnings on Feb 25 fall inside the 5-day horizon as the key binary catalyst, with AI-capex sentiment mixed: OpenAI tempered its compute-spend target to $600B and CoreWeave's Blue Owl financing failure raised data-center funding concerns, even as Alphabet's Gemini enterprise rollout restored some AI confidence. Core holdings drew positive analyst action (BofA raised CAT to $825 on turbine demand; Redburn raised WMT to $150), though several portfolio names are RSI-extended (CAT 73, GE 80, JNJ 76, PLD 71, TLT 73).

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift model over the actual 5-trading-day holding horizon (2026-02-20 to 2026-02-27), using only data through the decision date; p10/p90 are volatility-scaled interval bounds. Expected returns are small relative to intervals, so rankings should be judged on excess return vs the SPY benchmark (SPY expected +0.29%), not on sign vs zero: strongest excess are CAT +1.17, GLD +0.82, GOOGL +0.75, GE +0.72, JNJ +0.66, NVDA +0.45, XOM +0.38, NEE +0.35; weakest are AMZN -0.46, META -0.45, V -0.43, HD -0.37, MSFT -0.33, PG -0.32. Confidence is scaled from excess return per unit of interval width, so wide-interval names (LLY, NVDA, META at 37-48% annualized vol) carry near-neutral confidence despite positive drift. Limitations: the drift method extrapolates recent trend and does not model mean reversion, and several forecast leaders (CAT RSI 73, GE RSI 80, LIN RSI 72, JNJ RSI 76, PG RSI 71.5, PLD RSI 71, TLT RSI 73) are short-term overbought and prone to pullbacks the model will not flag; intervals are symmetric and understate fat tails; at a 5-day horizon idiosyncratic news and earnings surprises dominate, and no fundamental, news, or macro inputs are incorporated.

I trim the AI-capex cluster from ~34% to ~28% (NVDA 8.3→6.5, PLD 7→5) ahead of the Feb 25 NVDA binary given left-skewing capex signals (OpenAI tempering, CoreWeave financing stress), and hold ~19% cash as an explicit buffer for the binary event, fresh 10% global tariffs, and Iran strike risk; every other holding sits below the 20bps round-trip cost hurdle and is left untouched, with GE and JNJ held but not added despite high forecast drift given RSI 80/76.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-02-27 to 2026-03-06), using only price history up to the decision date; one forecast_universe call supplied all tickers. p10/p90 are 80% intervals derived from recent volatility; wide intervals reflect genuine 5-day uncertainty, not evidence to avoid an asset. Expected returns must be compared against the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.25% expected, 80% interval -3.14% to +3.76%), not against zero: on that basis the largest positive excess returns are CAT (+1.22%), GLD (+0.91%), GOOGL (+0.77%), JNJ (+0.72%), GE (+0.72%), XOM (+0.48%), NEE (+0.44%), while MSFT (-0.31%), HD (-0.34%), V (-0.43%), AMZN (-0.41%), META (-0.49%) screen weakest. Confidence is the approximate probability of outperforming SPY implied by the excess return and interval width, so all values sit near 0.5-0.6: over 5 days, idiosyncratic noise dominates and no forecast is high-confidence. Limitations: drift extrapolation captures momentum but not mean reversion or regime shifts; 30-day volatility windows may understate fat tails and event risk; no fundamental or news-based adjustment is incorporated; several names carry stretched short-term technicals (e.g., LIN RSI 88, SO RSI 73.5, TLT RSI 80.7, CVX/GE/JNJ at 52-week highs) where 5-day drift persistence is historically unreliable, so treat point estimates as weak signals and size positions against the interval widths.

decision.rationale: I keep the rotation core risk-sized rather than adopting the equal-third reference: CAT stays at 11% (38% vol, +31% over 90d) and GOOGL at 13% (below its 20/50-day but +95% 12-1m with positive data-center news), while GLD is trimmed to 9% because the critic showed its forecast interval is vol-inconsistent (confidence ~0.55) and its 30d return is negative at 49% vol. I deploy about 5% of the cash buffer into the cleanest trends — JNJ to 10% (52-week high, 13.7% vol, +0.72% expected excess), XOM to 10% plus new CVX 4% on the US-Iran oil escalation, and CAT to 11% on the Wells Fargo upgrade — while cutting NVDA to 3% (verified -9.4% two-day post-earnings drop, AI contagion), JPM to 3% and LLY to 2.5% on zero expected excess and headline/vol risk. The remaining 15.4% cash is explicit event-risk insurance for the unverified macro calendar and binary geopolitics inside the 5-day window; round-trip costs (~2bps on ~22% turnover) are small versus the ~45bps expected excess over a flat SPY.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-03-06 to next decision 2026-03-13), using only price history up to the decision date; one forecast per ticker, no post-date information. Benchmark SPY forecast: +0.25% expected (p10 -3.14, p90 +3.76). Excess returns vs SPY: CAT +1.13, GLD +0.82, GOOGL +0.75, GE +0.70, JNJ +0.55, XOM +0.41, NVDA +0.35, WMT/NEE +0.31, CVX +0.19, PLD +0.03, JPM/LLY/SO ~-0.01, LIN -0.12, AAPL -0.16, TLT -0.19, AMT -0.22, MSFT -0.21, AMZN -0.25, META/SHW -0.31, HD -0.33, PG -0.40, V -0.42. Confidence is scaled from the signal-to-noise ratio of excess return vs the p10-p90 interval width, so it is modest everywhere: at a 5-day horizon, expected returns are small relative to volatility-scaled intervals (e.g., NVDA p10-p90 spans -7.1% to +8.9%), and wide intervals are uncertainty, not evidence to avoid an asset. Limitations: drift/momentum extrapolation is noisy over 5 days and can whipsaw around short-term moving averages (several names sit just below SMA20); the model does not incorporate news, earnings, macro events, or regime shifts; p10/p90 assume approximately symmetric volatility-scaled distributions and may understate tail risk for high-vol names (LLY ~49%, GLD ~50%, MSFT ~42%, CAT ~42% annualized 30d vol). Relative ranking is more reliable than absolute levels: industrials/energy/gold (CAT, GE, XOM, GLD, JNJ, GOOGL) screen with the largest positive excess vs the benchmark, while consumer/defensive names (PG, V, HD, SHW) and TLT screen slightly below it.

decision.rationale: I reject the reference thirds: CAT is halved to 6% (RSI 23, decline accelerating despite +107% 12-1m) rather than tripled, GOOGL is trimmed to 11.5% for its live corrective phase below the 20/50-day SMAs plus regulatory risk, and GLD/XOM stay near current size as already-sized event hedges given the binary Hormuz outcome and XOM's verified non-response to the oil spike. Freed capital plus part of the cash goes where tape, forecast, and news agree — JNJ to 13% (lowest-vol uptrend, +17.7% 90d), GE to 6.5%, WMT to 8%, and modest SO/LIN adds on multi-horizon relative strength — while NVDA, LLY, and JPM are cut on broken trends and negative catalysts. The ~13% cash buffer is justified by observed risks (payrolls shock, war escalation, VIX 21) and total turnover (~32% of book, ~3bps cost) stays well inside the roughly 40bp forecast excess.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call; drift-based statistical forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-03-13 to 2026-03-20), using only data up to the decision date. p10/p90 are roughly 80% prediction intervals scaled from recent volatility; confidence is the estimated probability the direction call is correct (expected return divided by interval-implied sigma), so most calls are near coin-flip because 5-day expected moves are small relative to noise. Compare expected returns to the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.27%), not to zero: largest positive excess vs SPY are CAT +1.19, GOOGL +0.89, GLD +0.79, NVDA +0.62, XOM +0.51, GE +0.51, JNJ +0.50; largest negative excess are V -0.57, PG -0.51, HD -0.48, SHW -0.46, AMT -0.45, META -0.39, TLT -0.32. forecaster.method_notes: Forecasts are statistical drift-based estimates over the 5-trading-day horizon (2026-03-20 to next decision 2026-03-27), using only price history up to the decision date; no post-date information is used. Expected returns should be judged against the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.31%), not zero: on an excess basis the most favorable names are CAT (+1.04%), GOOGL (+0.85%), GLD (+0.54%), GE (+0.48%), XOM (+0.45%), JNJ (+0.40%), WMT (+0.30%), NVDA (+0.62%), CVX (+0.25%), while most others are flat-to-negative versus benchmark. Key limitations: (1) p10-p90 intervals are wide (roughly +/-3-7%) relative to point estimates under +/-1.5%, so all direction calls are weak and every interval straddles zero; wide intervals reflect high 30-day volatility and short-horizon noise, not a reason to avoid an asset. (2) The drift method does not model fundamentals, earnings, news, macro events, or regime shifts. (3) Extreme technical readings in the snapshot are not explicitly modeled: deeply oversold names (HD RSI 14.1, SHW 12.5, PG 14.9, GLD 14.8, V 20.8, LLY 20.0) could mean-revert upward or continue falling, and overbought energy names (CVX RSI 72.4, XOM 62.0 at 52-week highs) could extend or fade; the model's point estimates embed some momentum but treat these ambiguously. (4) Five-day returns are dominated by idiosyncratic noise, so confidence values are deliberately modest (0.35-0.55). (5) Transaction costs of 10 bps each way are not included in the return forecasts.

With 10 bps each-way costs against sub-1% expected excess returns, churn is limited to exiting confirmed downtrends; the defensive/relative-strength core stays put, and I expect roughly flat absolute performance with modest positive excess versus a flat benchmark.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the 9-trading-day horizon (decision 2026-03-27 to next decision 2026-04-10), using only price history up to the decision date; a single forecast_universe call supplied all tickers. SPY is included as the comparison-only benchmark anchor: expected +0.44% (p10 -4.01%, p90 +5.10%). Rank assets on excess return vs this benchmark, not vs zero. Leading excess: CAT +2.10pp, GOOGL +1.37pp, XOM +1.11pp, JNJ +1.02pp, GLD +0.98pp, WMT +0.79pp; lagging: AMT -1.11pp, PG -0.95pp, META -0.92pp, V -0.84pp, MSFT -0.71pp. Confidence is derived from a normal approximation fitted to each p10/p90 band: for up/down it is the estimated probability the return lands on the stated side of the SPY forecast; for flat it is the probability of finishing within +/-1pp of SPY (hence low flat confidences simply reflect wide 9-day distributions, not unreliable data). Limitations: (1) 9-day horizons have very low signal-to-noise - implied 1-sigma moves of roughly 2-8% mean most up/down confidences sit near 0.5-0.6 and wide p10-p90 intervals are uncertainty, not avoid-signals; (2) drift models extrapolate recent trends and can miss regime turns - several names sit at momentum extremes (MSFT/META/PG/LLY deeply oversold with RSI<20; XOM/CVX RSI>82 at 52-week highs; GLD in a sharp 30d correction at -13.2%) where mean-reversion or continuation risk is elevated and the point estimates may understate tail outcomes; (3) intervals assume approximately log-normal returns without jumps and do not incorporate news, earnings, or macro events inside the window; (4) expected edges of 0.5-2pp are small relative to 10bps each-way transaction costs and to interval width, so sizing should use the full distribution rather than the point estimate alone.

GE.notes: Chopping between the 20/200-day above and the 50-day below; 30d -5.17%, 90d -1.79%, 43% vol. 12-1m +92.99% is stale leadership; no current edge.

NEE.notes: Above all SMAs, -1% off 52-week high, 90d +19.16% with only 17.5% vol - but RSI 82 is the most extreme in the universe. Strong trend, severe 5-day mean-reversion risk.

SO.notes: Above all SMAs near 52-week highs with 14.7% vol; RSI 78.3 is overbought. Quality low-vol uptrend that is short-term stretched.

LIN.notes: At 52-week highs above all SMAs, outperforming SPY on 30d (+4.49%) and 90d (+14.82%), RSI 60.8 with room. One of the cleanest trend setups available.

SHW.notes: Sharp +4.14% 30-day rebound off lows but still below the 50/200-day SMAs with flat 12-1m (+3.86%); RSI 73.9. Bounce inside a larger downtrend, not a trend.

PLD.notes: Above all SMAs with 90d +7.71% and 12-1m +53.7%, -3.1% off high; RSI 77.5 is the main caution. Solid trend, overbought timing.

AMT.notes: Below 50/200-day SMAs, -21.4% off high, 12-1m -7.52%; holding above the 20-day. Weakest real-asset trend in the universe.

TLT.notes: Flat across all horizons (30d -0.35%, 90d +0.12%, 12-1m +2.7%), sitting on its 20/200-day cluster. Pure range; no signal either way.

GLD.notes: Violent whipsaw: -18% crash from the 3/2 high (490) to the 3/26 low (400.64), then +9% rebound to 437; below the 50-day, above the 20/200-day, RSI 62.8. Hedge failed its purpose; regime is unstable.

Overbought cluster across the winning book: NEE (RSI 82), SO (78.3), PLD (77.5), SHW (73.9), JPM (73.8), CAT (73), AMZN (75) - on a 5-trading-day horizon this concentration carries acute mean-reversion risk even inside intact uptrends.

GLD hedge dysfunction: the 3% position crashed -18% peak-to-trough in mid-March then rebounded +9%, still below its 50-day at 34% vol - it amplified regime risk rather than dampening it and its hedge value over the next week is unreliable.

Narrow benchmark leadership: SPY is near 52-week highs (RSI 68) with 90d still negative (-1.19%), so index gains depend on the same CAT/GOOGL/NVDA momentum complex the reference allocation concentrates in - if leadership cracks, both portfolio and benchmark fall together; high-vol names (GE 43%, META 45%, CAT 42%) magnify any crack.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call; statistical drift model fit only to price history through the 2026-04-10 decision date; horizon is 5 trading days (to next decision 2026-04-17). Benchmark SPY: expected +0.41% (p10 -2.94%, p90 +3.88%); rank names on excess return vs SPY, not on sign vs zero. Largest positive edges vs benchmark: CAT +1.32%, GOOGL +1.00%, NVDA +0.64%, GE +0.44%, GLD +0.43%, WMT +0.38%, JNJ +0.37%; most negative: AMT -0.70%, PG -0.64%, V -0.63%, MSFT -0.44%. Confidence = probability the stated call holds vs the benchmark under a normal approximation with sigma=(p90-p10)/2.56 (up: P(beat SPY); down: P(trail SPY); flat: P(within +/-1% of SPY)). Low confidence on flat calls reflects wide 5-day intervals (noise), not asset quality; wide p10-p90 bands are uncertainty, not avoid signals. Limitations: 5-day expected returns are small relative to daily volatility, so signal-to-noise is low and most edges are near or below the 10 bps each-way (20 bps round-trip) transaction cost, favoring trades only on the strongest excesses; the model is purely statistical (drift/momentum/volatility) and does not incorporate fundamentals, earnings, news, or geopolitical/event outcomes; intervals are marginal per-ticker and ignore cross-correlations; SPY is included for reference only (benchmark, comparison_only, not tradable).

decision.rationale: I act only on the edges that clear the 20bp round-trip cost: GOOGL to 17% (cleanest trend in the universe, RSI 60 with headroom, +1.00% excess), CAT doubled to 7% (top edge +1.32%, but capped well below the reference 33% because it sits ~10% above its 20-day at 42% vol with a thesis-specific Maine headline), and a new 5% NVDA tilt. I trim JNJ 13.4%->11% into its in-horizon earnings print since the statistical band excludes gap risk, cut the energy sleeve 12.1%->8.5% (XOM/CVX below 20/50-day SMAs with falling RSIs, slide active per verified anchors), and trim the RSI 78-82 NEE/SO cluster where 5-day mean-reversion risk meets below-cost edges. The 25% cash is now a priced decision, not a default: with the fragile ceasefire expiring just after the window, JNJ earnings inside it, and SPY at RSI 68, every remaining deployable candidate is either below cost (GE, WMT/LIN increments), in a downtrend (MSFT, V, META, HD, LLY, AMT), or overbought (JPM, AMZN, SHW), so cash plus the 3% GLD tail position (forecaster's top-5 edge, violent snap-back potential on a breakdown) is the cheapest available hedge.

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecasts over the 5-trading-day horizon (2026-04-17 to 2026-04-24), using only data available at the decision date. Benchmark: SPY expected +0.68% (p10 -2.39%, p90 +3.84%); all edges should be judged against this, not zero. Largest positive excess vs SPY: CAT +1.33%, GOOGL +0.99%, NVDA +0.80%, GE +0.50%; largest negative: AMT -0.96%, PG -0.84%, TLT -0.72%, HD -0.66%, V -0.64%. Confidence is the estimated probability of beating the benchmark, computed from the expected excess return scaled by the p10-p90 interval width (approximate Gaussian assumption); values cluster near 0.5 because 5-day expected edges are small relative to daily volatility. Limitations: (1) 5-day returns are noise-dominated, so wide p10-p90 intervals are uncertainty, not evidence to avoid an asset; (2) drift extrapolated from recent momentum can mean-revert, and many names (SPY RSI 96.7, AMZN 97.6, META 96.4, GOOGL 93.8, MSFT 92.8, NVDA 92.5) sit at extreme overbought readings after a sharp 30-day rally, raising pullback risk the drift model does not capture; (3) energy (XOM/CVX RSI 18-23) shows short-term oversold conditions that may bounce; (4) no fundamental, news, or earnings-event information is incorporated; (5) with 20bp round-trip transaction costs, only edges clearly above that threshold are actionable.

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day holding horizon (2026-04-24 to next decision 2026-05-01), using only price history through the decision date; SPY is included as the benchmark baseline (its confidence is P(positive return)). p10/p90 are volatility-scaled 80% intervals; wide intervals reflect 5-day noise, not a reason to avoid an asset. Confidence = estimated probability the ticker outperforms SPY over the horizon, derived from a normal approximation of each ticker's p10-p90 spread versus SPY's; values near 0.5 indicate low benchmark-relative conviction, which is normal at this horizon. Expected excess returns vs SPY: CAT +1.48%, GOOGL +0.95%, NVDA +0.64%, JNJ +0.26%, PLD +0.24%, GE +0.30%, XOM +0.20%, NEE +0.19%, CVX/AMZN/GLD +0.11%, WMT +0.09%, AAPL +0.04%, JPM -0.03%, META -0.15%, LLY -0.20%, LIN -0.28%, SO -0.44%, TLT -0.50%, SHW -0.56%, HD -0.63%, PG -0.74%, V -0.71%, MSFT -0.39%, AMT -0.86%. Limitations: (1) the drift model assumes momentum continuation and does not capture mean-reversion risk after sharp rallies - many names are short-term overbought (AMZN RSI 95, NVDA 87, SPY 88, GOOGL 83, CAT 84, META 81, MSFT 76, PLD 76), so upside expected returns may be overstated; (2) no fundamentals, earnings, news, or macro events are modeled despite news being available; (3) 5-day expected excess returns are small relative to both the forecast intervals and the 10 bps each-way transaction cost, so marginal edges (under ~0.2% excess) may not be net-positive to trade; (4) energy names (XOM, CVX) show oversold RSI with positive drift, a mixed signal the model does not reconcile; (5) single-model point estimates - actual outcomes will frequently fall outside p10-p90 for individual names.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call; statistical drift model fit only to data through the 2026-05-01 decision date, forecasting the 5-trading-day window to 2026-05-08. Expected returns and p10/p90 (80% intervals) come from the tool. Confidence is derived from a normal fit to each interval (sigma=(p90-p10)/2.563): for 'up' it is P(return>0), for 'down' P(return<0), for 'flat' P(|return|<=0.5%); all values are modest because 5-day returns are noise-dominated, and low 'flat' confidences reflect the improbability of landing inside a narrow band, not a weak forecast. Benchmark comparison (SPY expected +0.68%, p10 -1.62, p90 +3.02; SPY is comparison-only, not tradable): only CAT (+1.56pp), GOOGL (+1.20pp) and NVDA (+0.71pp) show meaningful positive expected excess; AAPL, WMT, JNJ, XOM, CVX, PLD, NEE, GE and AMZN sit within roughly +/-0.25pp of SPY (statistically indistinguishable); AMT (-0.96pp), PG (-0.85pp), HD (-0.76pp), SHW (-0.69pp), V (-0.62pp), TLT (-0.60pp), SO (-0.48pp), MSFT and LIN (-0.39pp), LLY (-0.35pp), META (-0.23pp) and GLD (-0.11pp) lag the benchmark. Limitations: pure drift/momentum extrapolation with no fundamental, news, or event modeling; several leaders are extremely extended (GOOGL RSI 86.8, AMZN 83.3, SPY 79.3, CAT 75.2, WMT 71.0), so short-horizon mean-reversion risk is understated by symmetric intervals; the normal approximation understates fat tails; earnings or macro events inside the window are not modeled; wide p10-p90 intervals represent uncertainty, not evidence that an asset should be avoided; expected 5-day edges for near-benchmark names are comparable to or smaller than round-trip transaction costs (10bps each way), so trading into them is not justified by the point forecast alone.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call; statistical drift model over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-05-08 to 2026-05-15), using only price history up to the decision date. Benchmark SPY is expected +0.59% (p10 -1.64, p90 +2.87); rank names on excess vs SPY, not on sign vs zero. Largest positive excess: CAT +1.52, GOOGL +1.20, NVDA +0.74; modest positive: JNJ/GE/NEE/PLD/AMZN/GLD/AAPL/WMT/XOM/CVX (+0.0 to +0.2); expected laggards: AMT -0.87, HD -0.77, PG -0.73, V -0.69, SHW -0.66, TLT -0.57, SO -0.51, MSFT -0.46, LLY/META -0.4, JPM -0.13. p10-p90 bands (roughly +/-2% to +/-7%) dwarf the 5-day expected moves; wide intervals are uncertainty about the outcome, not evidence an asset should be avoided. Confidence = Phi(excess/sd) with sd estimated from the p10-p90 band: the model's probability that the benchmark-relative direction call is realized; all values are modest (max 0.66 for TLT, driven by its low vol) because 5-day noise dominates drift. Limitations: purely price-statistical drift with no news, fundamentals, or earnings-event inputs; it assumes recent momentum persists, so extended names (GOOGL RSI 89, AMZN 80, CAT 72, SPY 74) carry gap/mean-reversion risk the model does not capture; 5-day expected edges are small relative to 10 bps-each-way transaction costs, so benchmark-relative differences of a few tenths of a percent should not be over-traded.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day holding horizon (2026-05-15 to next decision 2026-05-22), using only price history up to the decision date; p10/p90 are volatility-scaled percentile bands from estimated 30d annualized vol. Expected returns should be judged against the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.55%), not zero: on excess-return basis the strongest names are CAT (+1.44%), GOOGL (+1.17%), NVDA (+0.78%), XOM (+0.35%), AAPL (+0.26%), JNJ (+0.24%), CVX (+0.20%), NEE (+0.18%); weakest are AMT (-1.00%), HD (-0.88%), SHW (-0.88%), PG (-0.72%), V (-0.66%), MSFT (-0.60%), TLT (-0.55%), META (-0.50%), SO (-0.46%). Limitations: (1) 5-day expected returns are small relative to the p10-p90 bands, so all directional signals are weak and wide intervals reflect genuine uncertainty, not avoidability; (2) the drift method assumes short-horizon momentum continuation and does not model mean reversion from stretched conditions (AAPL RSI 88.5, GOOGL RSI 76.9, LLY RSI 75.2, SPY RSI 69.9), which is a downside risk for the highest-momentum names; (3) no fundamental, news, earnings, or macro inputs are incorporated despite news being available; (4) percentile bands assume approximately symmetric return distributions and may understate left-tail risk for high-vol names (CAT 44%, GE 44.7%, LLY 40.4% annualized vol); (5) confidence is a qualitative 0-1 score combining signal magnitude, excess return vs benchmark, and interval tightness, not a calibrated probability.

Core holdings look well-supported: Evercore raised its Caterpillar target to $1,103 on AI power demand, GOOGL/NVDA were the standout Mag-7 earnings reports, Prologis raised its 2026 development outlook with a data-center expansion, and JNJ beat and raised guidance. Offsetting risks: consumer stress signals (gas up 42% YoY, Walmart's cautious tone and pledged price cuts), rising borrowing costs with Fed rate-hike chatter pressuring TLT and GLD, and NextEra's proposed $116B mostly-stock Dominion deal adding event risk to utilities.

AMT.notes: Sideways rebound: +2.7% 30d lags SPY, price back above the 20/50-day but still under the 200-day. 12-1 -13.2% is negative; recovery is early-stage.

TLT.notes: Mild downtrend below all SMAs, -4.6% 90d lags SPY. 9.4% vol is the lowest in the universe, but it currently offers neither momentum nor defensive ballast.

GLD.notes: Correction within a longer uptrend: -14.0% 90d and -4.0% 30d lag SPY, price below the 20/50-day but holding above the 200-day. 12-1 +41.0% keeps the big trend alive but short-term momentum has rolled over.

risks: AAPL RSI 91.3 is extreme overbought at 52-week highs; +13.1% 30d momentum is real but 4-day mean-reversion risk is high — positive expected return does not imply outperformance at this stretch.
SPY itself is stretched (RSI 72.1, 0.3% off highs, 10.6% vol) — a benchmark pullback would hit the portfolio's high-beta core (GOOGL, NVDA, CAT, LLY) hardest.
Concentration plus volatility: GOOGL (14.7%), NVDA (11.4%) and CAT (9.0%) all run 37-42% annualized vol vs SPY's 10.6%; the book is effectively a leveraged bet on continued risk-on.
GOOGL has faded four straight sessions from 396 to 382.5 and closed below its SMA20 — short-term momentum has cooled even though the larger trend is up; adding into the fade is not free.
Broad laggard cluster: HD, SHW, PG, META, MSFT, TLT and GLD all lag SPY on 30d and 90d with negative or broken momentum — few safe rotation destinations outside cash.
GLD's 90d -14.0% shows its momentum regime has rolled over despite +41% 12-1, and TLT below all SMAs provides no rate-hedge ballast — hedges are absent in this universe.
High-vol event risk into a 4-day window: LLY, GE, NEE, NVDA, CAT all exceed 33% vol, and 10bps cost each way makes churn expensive — sizing discipline matters more than signal churn.

forecaster.method_notes: Forecasts generated by forecast_universe (drift-based statistical model) using only data through the 2026-05-22 decision date, over the actual 4-trading-day holding horizon to 2026-05-29. expected_return_pct is the expected price change over the horizon; p10_pct/p90_pct span an 80% predictive interval. SPY (expected +0.4%) is the comparison benchmark, included for reference; all directional calls should be judged on excess return vs SPY, not vs zero. Confidence is derived from the probability of outperforming the SPY forecast implied by each ticker's interval width (sigma approx (p90-p10)/2.56); values cluster near 0.5 because 4-day expected excess returns are small relative to short-horizon volatility. Largest positive excess vs benchmark: CAT (+1.08), GOOGL (+0.98), NVDA (+0.47), AAPL (+0.2), XOM (+0.21); most negative: HD (-0.65), SHW (-0.61), PG (-0.52), V (-0.51), AMT (-0.53), MSFT (-0.49), META (-0.47), TLT (-0.36). Limitations: (1) the drift method extrapolates recent trend/momentum and does not model earnings, macro events, news, or regime shifts; (2) overbought conditions (AAPL RSI 91.3, SPY RSI 72.1, LLY 70.9, PLD 71.4) create mean-reversion risk not captured by the model; (3) 30-day volatility windows may understate event-week risk; (4) wide p10-p90 intervals reflect genuine 4-day uncertainty, not evidence to avoid an asset; (5) returns are gross of the 10 bps each-way transaction costs; (6) single forecast per ticker, no ensemble or scenario weighting.

decision.rationale: I keep the GOOGL/CAT/NVDA core (best multi-horizon momentum, RSI 50/52/64 with headroom) but do not add: verified prices show all three cooled this week, and NVDA's blowout quarter was met with -4.3% selling, so I trim NVDA to 9.5% and AAPL 7.3%→4.5% (RSI 91.3 against only +0.2% forecast excess). I exit WMT (unexplained ~10% post-earnings leg down, fresh negative news) and NEE (dilutive $116B mostly-stock Dominion deal is an unhedged coin-flip with zero forecast edge), and let cash rise to ~31.5% as the only functioning hedge with SPY at RSI 72 after eight straight weekly gains and no lagging alternative worth rotating into; the ~16% turnover costs only ~2bps. This departs from the equal-thirds CAT/GOOGL/JNJ reference because 100% in three 37-42%-vol names into a stretched benchmark is uncompensated concentration risk, while the 68%-invested book keeps the momentum premium and outperforms SPY in flat-to-down scenarios.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day holding horizon (2026-05-29 to next decision 2026-06-05), using only price history up to the decision date; one forecast_universe call supplied all tickers. Expected returns are small relative to the p10-p90 intervals, which are calibrated to recent 30-day volatility: at a 5-day horizon, drift signal is weak versus noise, so all rankings are low-conviction. Confidence is the estimated probability the ticker beats the SPY benchmark expected return (0.49%), derived from the implied distribution (sigma approx (p90-p10)/2.56); values cluster near 0.5, correctly signaling little separation. Relative to SPY, the largest positive excess forecasts are CAT (+1.30pp), GOOGL (+1.13pp), JNJ (+0.35pp), NVDA (+0.37pp), AAPL (+0.27pp), LLY (+0.26pp); widest downside among these are NVDA/LLY/CAT (p10 near -4 to -6%), while JNJ offers the best excess-to-width tradeoff (p10 -2.11%). Limitations: (1) drift models extrapolate recent trends and do not capture mean reversion in overextended names (AAPL RSI 84.3, LLY RSI 81.1, SPY RSI 68.8), which is a known risk for the top-momentum names; (2) no fundamental, news, earnings, or macro inputs beyond price history; (3) 5-day returns are dominated by idiosyncratic noise, so wide intervals are uncertainty about outcomes, not evidence an asset should be avoided; (4) expected excess returns of 0.1-1.3pp are of the same order as round-trip transaction costs (20bps), so small forecast edges should not be traded aggressively; (5) quantiles assume approximately symmetric (log-normal) return distributions and may understate tail risk for high-vol names (CAT 42.5%, LLY 42.4%, NVDA 38.6% annualized vol).

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-06-05 to 2026-06-12), from a single forecast_universe call using only decision-date history; SPY included as the comparison-only benchmark. p10/p90 are 80% intervals scaled from recent volatility; wide intervals reflect short-horizon noise, not a reason to avoid an asset. Compare expected returns to the SPY benchmark (+0.49%, p10 -1.69, p90 +2.72), not to zero. Expected excess vs SPY: CAT +1.42pp, GOOGL +1.04pp, LLY +0.42pp, AAPL +0.40pp, JNJ +0.39pp, NVDA +0.38pp, XOM +0.30pp, PLD +0.21pp, CVX +0.20pp, GE +0.18pp, NEE +0.04pp, GLD -0.01pp (in line); negative excess: WMT -0.07, AMZN -0.10, JPM -0.10, LIN -0.26, SO -0.37, TLT -0.39, MSFT -0.62, META -0.59, AMT -0.59, V -0.65, PG -0.67, HD -0.73, SHW -0.75. Confidence is a normal-approximation probability that the signed drift realizes (P(ret>0) for up, P(ret<0) for down; flat calls set to neutral 0.50); all values sit in 0.50-0.65, so no call is high conviction. Limitations: 5-day returns are noise-dominated (typical 1-sigma of 2-4% vs expected moves under 2%), drift extrapolates recent momentum and can mean-revert or whipsaw, no news/earnings/macro events or regime shifts are modeled, intervals assume roughly log-normal returns, and at 10bps each-way transaction costs, excess edges below ~0.5pp are not reliably tradable.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift model (single forecast_universe call) using only data through the 2026-06-12 decision date; horizon is 9 trading days to the 2026-06-26 rebalance. SPY is the benchmark (comparison only, not tradable): expected +0.82%, p10 -2.11%, p90 +3.85%. Rank names on excess vs SPY, not on sign vs zero: CAT +2.65, GOOGL +1.85, JNJ +0.80, LLY +0.66, NVDA +0.59, XOM +0.53, AAPL +0.48, CVX +0.39, PLD +0.39, GE +0.26 are above benchmark; NEE (-0.01), GLD (-0.07), JPM (-0.08), WMT (-0.12) are essentially in line; MSFT (-1.37) and META (-1.39) are most negative, with AMZN, HD, PG, V, SO, LIN, SHW, AMT, TLT also below. Confidence = P(stated direction) from a normal fit to the tool's p10/p90 band (sigma = (p90-p10)/2.565); for 'flat' calls it is P(|return| < 2%). forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 9-trading-day horizon (2026-06-26 to 2026-07-10), using only data available at the decision date; one forecast_universe call supplied all tickers. Expected returns should be judged against the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.75%), not zero: on excess-return basis the strongest names are CAT (+2.92pp), GOOGL (+1.57pp), JNJ (+1.03pp), GE (+0.82pp), LLY (+0.63pp), AAPL (+0.55pp); the weakest are MSFT (-1.56pp), META (-1.48pp), AMT (-1.32pp), V (-0.89pp), PG (-0.90pp). Confidence is a signal-to-noise score: |expected excess vs SPY| relative to the p10-p90 half-width, so it is modest (0.50-0.66) everywhere because 9-day intervals are dominated by volatility. Wide p10-p90 ranges (e.g., NVDA -7.2% to +10.1%, LLY -7.6% to +11.2%) are uncertainty about the path, not evidence an asset should be avoided; JNJ, TLT, SO, and LIN have the tightest distributions. Limitations: single-method drift model assumes recent trend persistence and can whipsaw at inflection points; volatility is estimated from a 30-day window and may understate regime shifts or event risk (e.g., GOOGL's flagged dilutive raise, CAT's stretched valuation at 49% vol); no fundamental, news, or earnings-event modeling is embedded; RSI/overbought conditions (HD 73, GE 74, JNJ 73, SHW 72) and oversold conditions (GOOGL 29.5, XOM 26.6, CVX 27) are not explicitly mean-reversion-adjusted; 9 trading days is short, so point estimates carry wide error bands and rankings within ~0.5pp of the benchmark are statistically indistinguishable.

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecasts over the 5-trading-day horizon (2026-07-10 to next decision 2026-07-17), using only price history up to the decision date; no post-date information, fundamentals, or news are incorporated. Expected returns are small relative to the p10-p90 intervals, so rankings should be based on excess return versus the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.42% expected, range -1.81% to +2.70%) rather than on sign alone: CAT (+1.37% excess), GOOGL (+0.93%), JNJ (+0.64%), LLY (+0.42%), AAPL (+0.46%) screen best; MSFT (-0.89%), AMT (-0.84%), META (-0.59%) screen worst. Wide intervals reflect 30-day annualized volatility (e.g., CAT 54%, META 54%, NVDA 43%) and are uncertainty, not evidence to avoid an asset. Limitations: 5-day drift signals are weak and noise-dominated; volatility estimated from a 30-day window may not capture regime shifts or event risk (earnings, macro releases); the model assumes no jumps and treats the p50 as the drift midpoint, so fat-tail outcomes are understated; confidence is heuristic, scaled by interval width and recent volatility (higher for low-vol assets like TLT, SO, LIN, SPY; lower for high-vol CAT, META, NVDA).

research.summary: Markets enter the July 17 decision date in a tech-led drawdown: the S&P 500 fell ~1.6% for the week with the Nasdaq down 1.4% Friday, as a semiconductor rout deepened on TSMC's higher 2026 capex guidance, China's Kimi K3 AI model challenging the US AI lead, and Netflix's guidance disappointment. Alphabet's Q2 report on July 22 lands inside the 5-trading-day horizon and its capex guidance is flagged as the key swing factor for battered AI stocks, while the EU's DMA order to open Android/search data to AI rivals adds a regulatory overhang. Rotation is visible into financials (JPM set to raise its dividend ~10% after clearing the Fed stress test, at record highs), healthcare (LLY's $2.8B AtaiBeckley acquisition, UBS positive on GLP-1 moat), and energy (oil jumping on Middle East conflict, Chevron/ConocoPhillips pursuing Iraq deals). Technical extremes stand out: AAPL at an all-time high with RSI 88.7, and CAT down 20% from its June 30 high in a technical bear market at ~53% volatility.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-07-17 to 2026-07-24), using only price history up to the decision date; p10/p90 are 80% intervals from estimated volatility. Compare expected returns to the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.37%), not to zero: on that basis the largest positive excesses are CAT (+1.23pp, but widest interval and RSI 31.6 below its SMA20, so confidence capped), GOOGL (+0.94pp), JNJ (+0.63pp, tightest interval of the up names), AAPL (+0.54pp, though RSI 88.7 at 52-week highs raises mean-reversion risk), LLY (+0.46pp), PLD (+0.36pp), GE (+0.30pp), XOM (+0.24pp), CVX (+0.17pp); MSFT (-0.81pp), AMT (-0.79pp) and META (-0.57pp) screen worst vs benchmark. Limitations: 5-day drift is small relative to daily volatility, so intervals are wide and most names are statistically 'flat' vs the benchmark; the drift model does not capture mean reversion from RSI extremes (AAPL 88.7, XOM/CVX ~73, TLT 19.7), event risk (earnings, macro releases within the window), or fundamental/news catalysts; confidence values reflect signal-to-noise (excess return vs interval width) blended with technical context and are deliberately modest (0.41-0.60) given the short horizon. Wide intervals are uncertainty, not a reason to avoid an asset; with 10bps transaction costs each way, sub-0.3pp excess edges are not worth trading.

decision.rationale: I again reject the 33/33/33 reference: CAT's short-term trend is broken (below SMA20/50, RSI 31.6, 52.8% vol, valuation flagged rich) so I trim it to 9.5% despite the forecaster's top drift excess, and GOOGL's July-22 earnings sit inside the window as a binary gap, so I size it at 7.5% for event risk rather than its +1.31% point estimate. I rotate those proceeds plus part of the cash into the calls where all reports converge — JNJ, LLY, PLD (bullish SMA alignment, positive excess vs SPY, non-extended RSI) — trim AAPL to 10% on RSI-88.7 extension while respecting its multi-horizon strength, and cut NVDA on the deepening semiconductor rout. Per the critic I reject V and TLT additions (negative forecast excess), keep JPM/GE/energy/utilities as-is, and hold ~12% cash as justified ballast against the earnings event and breadth deterioration; net expected excess vs SPY is roughly +0.35pp after sub-1bp of turnover costs.

forecaster.method_notes: Forecasts are 5-trading-day statistical drift projections (decision date 2026-07-24 through next decision 2026-07-31) from forecast_universe, using only price history up to the decision date. Benchmark SPY: expected +0.35% (p10 -1.90%, p90 +2.65%); the decision-relevant metric is excess vs SPY, not absolute return. Expected excess vs SPY: CAT +1.20%, GOOGL +0.75%, JNJ +0.70%, AAPL +0.56%, LLY +0.44%, XOM +0.33%, PLD +0.29%, GE +0.24%, CVX +0.21%, NVDA +0.10%, JPM +0.08%, NEE +0.05%, GLD +0.01%, WMT -0.08%, LIN -0.15%, SO -0.19%, AMZN -0.30%, V -0.31%, TLT -0.32%, PG -0.36%, SHW -0.49%, HD -0.50%, META -0.71%, AMT -0.83%, MSFT -0.87%. confidence = estimated probability the ticker outperforms SPY over the horizon (normal approximation; per-ticker sigma from the p10/p90 band, sigma=(p90-p10)/2.563; assumed 0.75 correlation with SPY for equities, near 0 for TLT/GLD); for down names such as MSFT and AMT, low confidence means high probability of underperformance. Limitations: 5-day drift signals are weak relative to volatility - even the strongest calls (JNJ 0.65, CAT 0.61, AAPL/GOOGL 0.59) are only modestly better than a coin flip, so sizing should be diversified; wide p10-p90 intervals reflect genuine uncertainty, not proof an asset should be avoided; the drift model uses no news, fundamentals, or event risk and may miss mean reversion after extreme short-term moves (e.g., CVX RSI 92, XOM RSI 84, GOOGL RSI 27, TLT RSI 21); correlation assumptions are crude; with 10 bps transaction costs each way, expected excess edges under roughly 0.2% are not reliably tradable.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-07-31 to next decision 2026-08-07), using only price history up to the decision date; one forecast_universe call supplied all tickers. Benchmark SPY is expected +0.35% (p10 -1.93, p90 +2.69) over the same horizon, so relative comparisons should use excess returns: strongest are CAT (+1.00%), GOOGL (+0.87%), JNJ (+0.56%), LLY (+0.46%), XOM (+0.42%), AAPL (+0.38%); weakest are META (-0.82%), AMT (-0.79%), MSFT (-0.51%), HD (-0.48%), PG (-0.43%). All excess spreads are small relative to the 80% intervals (roughly +/-3-7% for single names), so no forecast is a high-conviction call; wide intervals reflect 5-day volatility and are uncertainty, not evidence to avoid an asset. Confidence is scored from signal-to-noise (|expected return| / half-width of the p10-p90 band) and is uniformly modest (0.30-0.40) because short-horizon drift has low signal-to-noise. Limitations: (1) drift extrapolation assumes recent trend/momentum persistence and can whipsaw around earnings, macro prints, or news within the 5-day window; (2) intervals are volatility-scaled and approximately symmetric, likely understating fat-tail/event risk (e.g., MSFT RSI 75, XOM/CVX RSI ~74 mean-reversion risk; META/LIN RSI ~23 oversold bounce potential); (3) no fundamentals, valuation, news, or cross-sectional factor modeling is incorporated; (4) 5-day expected returns are near zero for most names, so ranking is fragile to estimation error and transaction costs (10 bps each way) can consume a large share of the projected excess.

decision.rationale: I again reject the 33/33/33 reference: CAT and LLY face binary Q2 prints inside the 5-day window that the drift forecast cannot price, so I cut CAT to 3% (broken 30d trend, RSI 28.2, 52% vol) and LLY to 6.5%, while keeping the clean momentum core — GOOGL 12% (universe-best 12-1m, verified +6.7% Friday on revived AI confidence), JNJ ~14% (highest-confidence forecast, tightest band), JPM 10.5% — plus modest new V/AMZN exposure on confirmed uptrends near 52-week highs. I exit LIN and SO (broken/flat trends, zero forecast edge) and hold ~21% cash as the only technically supported de-risking tool (TLT and GLD both declining) against the earnings binaries and AI-rotation risk, accepting a trivial ~0.07% expected drag versus SPY's +0.35%. Turnover (~29% one-way, ~3bps cost) is concentrated in event-risk reduction and broken-trend exits, not cosmetic rebalancing, leaving expected excess of roughly +0.2% net of costs.

forecaster.method_notes: Single forecast_universe call; drift-based statistical model fit to each ticker's history through the 2026-08-07 decision date, evaluated over the actual 5-trading-day holding horizon (to 2026-08-14). All returns must be compared with the SPY benchmark forecast (expected +0.40%, p10 -1.92%, p90 +2.77%), not with zero. Excess vs benchmark: leaders CAT +0.91pp, GOOGL +0.79pp, JNJ +0.51pp, LLY +0.36pp, AAPL +0.35pp; laggards AMT -0.83pp, META -0.76pp, MSFT -0.43pp, TLT -0.38pp, SO -0.37pp. Confidence is derived from a normal approximation fitted to each p10/p90 band: for up/down names it is the probability of landing on the stated side of SPY's expected return; for flat names it measures benchmark-neutrality (2 x min(P(over), P(under))), NOT price stability - magnitude risk is in the p10/p90 spread, so a 0.99-confidence flat name like NVDA still carries a roughly -6%/+7% band. Limitations: (1) 5-day expected returns are small relative to interval widths (equity bands span ~6-14pp); wide intervals are normal short-horizon noise, not evidence to avoid an asset. (2) The largest excess return vs SPY is under 1pp, well inside model noise, so the ranking is low-conviction and moderate sizing with 10bps-each-way transaction costs in mind is appropriate. (3) The drift model cannot price binary event risk (earnings or macro prints inside the window), regime shifts, or news; names with stretched short-term momentum (MSFT RSI 81 after +30% in 30d, GLD RSI 73, SHW RSI 70) carry fatter left tails than the symmetric band implies. (4) Bands assume approximately log-normal returns and stable volatility over the horizon.

decision.rationale: I again reject the 33/33/33 reference: the forecaster itself admits all excess returns are sub-1pp inside noise, while CAT's near-term trend is broken (-10.1% 30d, below SMA-20/50, prominent Burry short despite record Q2) and GOOGL shows -10.9% 90d with an unpriced antitrust tail, so I hold CAT at 3% and trim GOOGL 11.6%->9% to cut the flagged concentration rather than chase the forecast ranking. The 17% cash buffer plus 2.5% GLD is deliberate insurance against the observed crowded-leader unwind risk (SPY RSI 69.6 at 52-week highs, Dimon leverage warning, Burry AI shorts), costing only ~0.07pp of expected drag versus SPY's +0.40% forecast while turnover costs are a negligible ~1.4bps.

forecaster.method_notes: Forecasts come from one forecast_universe call (statistical drift model) over the brief's actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-08-14 to 2026-08-21), using only data through the decision date; direction, expected_return_pct, p10_pct, and p90_pct are the tool's outputs. Confidence is my normal-approximation reading of signal strength: sigma=(p90-p10)/2.5632, with confidence=P(r>0) for up, P(r<0) for down, and P(|r|<=1%) for flat, so low flat-confidence means 'movement likely, direction unknown,' not 'avoid.' Key limitation: every expected return is small relative to its interval, and versus the SPY benchmark (expected +0.42%) no excess return exceeds +0.92pp (CAT) or falls below -0.94pp (META) - all edges are well inside 5-day noise, supporting at most mild tilts rather than high-conviction positions. The drift method does not model mean-reversion risk in extended names (MSFT RSI 86, NVDA 76, SPY 75), oversold bounces (AAPL RSI 27, SO 28), news/events, or fat tails; intervals assume near-normal returns and likely understate tail risk. Note the 12-minus-1-month reference names (CAT/LLY/GOOGL) coincide with the largest positive excess forecasts (+0.92/+0.43/+0.70pp), but those edges are also sub-1pp and inside noise.

decision.rationale: I again reject the 33/33/33 reference: CAT (6% below SMA-50, -19.4% off high, 90d -6.7%) and GOOGL (below SMA-50, 90d -13.7%) have damaged near-term trends and every forecast edge is sub-1pp inside 5-day noise, so both stay at hold-only 3%/8.7% while I tilt cash into multi-horizon strength instead - XOM/CVX (positive 30d/90d/12-1, RSI 61-62 unstretched, crude climbing), GE (+26.5% 90d, RSI 54.9) and LLY (+17.6% 90d, RSI 48) - and cut AAPL to 3.5% on its observed breakdown (RSI 27, below SMA-20/50, Jefferies cut to $263.66), keeping 3.5% for oversold-bounce optionality above SMA-200. Key limitation: every expected return is small relative to its interval, and versus the SPY benchmark (expected +0.42%) no excess return exceeds +0.92pp (CAT) or falls below -0.94pp (META) - all edges are well inside 5-day noise, supporting at most mild tilts rather than high-conviction positions. The drift method does not model mean-reversion risk in extended names (MSFT RSI 86, NVDA 76, SPY 75), oversold bounces (AAPL RSI 27, SO 28), news/events, or fat tails; intervals assume near-normal returns and likely understate tail risk. Note the 12-minus-1-month reference names (CAT/LLY/GOOGL) coincide with the largest positive excess forecasts (+0.92/+0.43/+0.70pp), but those edges are also sub-1pp and inside noise."}

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-08-21 to next decision 2026-08-28), using only price history up to the decision date; p10/p90 are 80% prediction intervals from recent volatility. Benchmark SPY is forecast at +0.38% (p10 -1.91, p90 +2.72); all expected returns should be compared against that, not zero. Largest positive edges vs SPY: CAT +1.01pp, LLY +0.96pp, GOOGL +0.67pp, XOM +0.56pp, JNJ +0.52pp; largest negative edges: META -1.01pp, HD -0.61pp, AMT -0.61pp, TLT -0.42pp, SO -0.42pp. Every edge is small (mostly within ~1pp) relative to interval widths of 3-14pp, so these are weak signals, not certainties; wide intervals reflect genuine 5-day uncertainty, not proof an asset should be avoided. Confidence is scaled by the edge-to-volatility ratio and is deliberately modest (0.35-0.60) for a short horizon. Limitations: drift models have low signal-to-noise over 5 days; they do not capture event risk (earnings, macro releases), mean-reversion after momentum/RSI extremes (e.g., GLD RSI 82.5, JNJ 72.1, XOM 70.2, CVX 70.3 near highs; GOOGL/AMZN/SO RSI <30 oversold), regime shifts, or fundamental news; and with 10bps transaction costs each way, sub-0.5pp forecast edges can be fully consumed by a round-trip trade, so positions should only be changed when the edge clearly exceeds costs.

I hold JNJ/XOM/CVX/JPM despite RSI ~70 because their multi-horizon trends beat SPY near 52-week highs (guidance: don't dismiss winners on RSI alone), keep GOOGL/NVDA/AMZN at current size rather than adding to a falling knife or ahead of the Aug-26 NVDA binary, and retain ~16% cash as cheap insurance (~5bp drag) against that earnings event and the reversible Hormuz/gold drivers. Turnover is minimal (~4%, ~0.4bp cost) since every remaining forecast edge is sub-1pp against a 20bp round trip.

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day horizon (2026-08-28 to 2026-09-04), using only price history through the decision date; one forecast_universe call, no per-ticker repeats. Benchmark SPY is expected +0.37% (p10 -1.91, p90 +2.70); rank assets by excess vs this benchmark, not by sign of expected return. Largest positive excess: CAT +0.93, GOOGL +0.67, LLY +0.65, JNJ +0.50, XOM +0.43; largest negative excess: META -0.91, AMT -0.57, HD -0.66, SO -0.41, SHW -0.43. p10/p90 are volatility-scaled 80% intervals: wide bands are uncertainty about magnitude, not evidence to avoid a name, and tight bands (TLT, SO, PG) reflect low vol, not high edge. Confidence is the implied probability the stated direction is correct (from expected return scaled by interval width); all values sit near 0.5 because a 5-day drift signal is weak relative to noise. Limitations: (1) drift models extrapolate recent trend and miss regime breaks, gap risk, and event risk (earnings, macro prints) within the window; (2) momentum-crash structures like CAT (-24.7% off high, below SMA-50) and META (-25.7% off high) can look attractive to a drift model precisely when crash risk is elevated; (3) no news or fundamental inputs were integrated; (4) most forecast edges (0.2-1.0%) are of the same order as round-trip transaction costs of 20bps, so forecasts favor minimal turnover and only high-conviction, benchmark-relative tilts.

Energy is the standout strength: crude near $104 on Iran-driven tensions with record $108 diesel margins, and Chevron's reset Venezuela JV terms support over $7B of planned investment. The AI trade is showing cracks (Broadcom down ~15% over the past month despite strong Q3 results, Marvell's Google custom-chip revenue deferred to fiscal 2029, a 'historic split' among the Magnificent Seven), while JNJ — the portfolio's largest holding at 18.5% — sits near its 52-week high but absorbed a fresh Louisiana talc verdict. GE won a $2.87B Navy engine contract yet is down ~12.7% over the past month, and LLY is down 2.7% since its earnings report amid intensifying obesity-drug competition.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 4-trading-day horizon (2026-09-04 to next decision 2026-09-11), using only price history up to the decision date; one forecast_universe call supplied all tickers. Expected returns should be judged against the SPY benchmark forecast of +0.30% (excess returns: CAT +0.70, LLY +0.49, GOOGL +0.46, JNJ +0.42, XOM +0.30, AAPL +0.24, CVX +0.19, GLD +0.12, NVDA/GE/PLD/JPM ~+0.03 to +0.09, V -0.18, AMZN -0.11, WMT -0.12, NEE -0.09, MSFT -0.30, PG/SO/LIN/TLT -0.28 to -0.35, SHW -0.43, AMT -0.52, HD -0.62, META -0.60). Limitations: (1) with only 4 trading days, expected drift is small relative to the p10-p90 bands, which scale with 30-day annualized volatility (e.g., NVDA/CAT/META bands span roughly 12%); wide intervals are uncertainty, not evidence to avoid an asset. (2) The drift model is purely quantitative price history; it does not incorporate news, earnings catalysts, or fundamentals within the window. (3) Short-horizon momentum can mean-revert, so point estimates carry low confidence; most names are effectively flat vs the benchmark. (4) With 10 bps transaction costs each way, expected excess returns under ~0.2% are unlikely to cover round-trip costs, so trading should concentrate on the largest positive excess-return names (CAT, LLY, GOOGL, JNJ, XOM, AAPL) and away from the clearest negative-excess names (HD, META, AMT, SHW).

decision.rationale: I reject the reference and the forecaster's top picks as stale 12-1 drift: CAT and GOOGL are momentum crashes below their 20/50-day SMAs and LLY's catalyst has faded, so I exit GOOGL, GE and AMZN, trim LLY to 3%, and cut JNJ from 18.5% to 15% to reduce the unpriced talc-verdict shock risk on the largest position. I redeploy into confirmed multi-horizon leaders — CVX and XOM on the strongest tape in the universe with the Iran-driven crude/refining catalyst, plus AAPL, NVDA, V, and a 4% GLD haven — while keeping ~27% cash because the blowout jobs report into the September FOMC is the dominant observed risk and most remaining deployments fail the 20bps round-trip cost bar. Against a flat SPY (+0.30% drift, RSI 47.7), the energy/healthcare/financials rotation should deliver modest net outperformance over the 4-day window.

Core holdings have fresh catalysts: JPM guided Q3 investment banking/markets revenue up mid-to-high teens, Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro with bullish analyst targets (Evercore $380), and JNJ carries strong momentum offset by STELARA biosimilar erosion, while LLY faces a binary September 30 obesity-combo (eloraTZP) readout inside the evaluation window. forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts (forecast_universe) for the actual 5-trading-day holding horizon (decision 2026-09-18 to next decision 2026-09-25; evaluation cutoff 2026-10-02), using only data through the decision date; p10/p90 are ~80% intervals with implied sigma = (p90-p10)/2.564. Rank names by excess vs the SPY benchmark forecast (+0.34% expected; p10 -1.95, p90 +2.67), not vs zero. Largest positive excess vs SPY: CAT +0.94, LLY +0.54, JNJ +0.51, XOM +0.49, GOOGL +0.44, AAPL +0.34, CVX +0.33, NVDA +0.20; HD is the only down name (-0.93 excess). JNJ shows the best risk-adjusted excess (tightest band); CAT's top raw excess carries the widest band (p10 -5.64 to p90 +8.71) after a -17.8% 90-day drawdown, so treat it as low conviction. Confidence definition: up/down = P(return beats/loses to SPY) under a normal approximation with assumed 0.70 return correlation to SPY (0.10 for TLT/GLD); flat = 1-|2P-1|, i.e., confidence there is no excess-return edge vs the benchmark - high flat confidence means expected to track SPY in expectation, NOT low risk (see p10/p90 for risk). SPY is included as the benchmark anchor with confidence 0.5 (not applicable). Limitations: at a 5-day horizon noise dominates drift, so directional confidences are modest (0.52-0.64) and point estimates have limited predictive power; symmetric intervals may understate tail risk (no earnings/event conditioning around the quarter-end window); constant-correlation and single-factor benchmark comparisons ignore sector/factor structure; with 10 bps transaction costs each way, excesses under ~0.3% are marginal after costs. Wide intervals are uncertainty, not proof that an asset should be avoided.

decision.rationale: I keep the proven JNJ/XOM/CVX/JPM/AAPL core and reject the reference CAT/LLY tilt and the forecaster's CAT/GOOGL top picks as stale 12-1 momentum artifacts contradicted by live downtrends, while deploying roughly half of the previously unaddressed 33% cash sleeve into the only names with multi-horizon relative strength and clearly net-of-cost excess (JNJ to 25% for the best risk-adjusted band, AAPL to 12% on persistent 30d/90d/12-1m leadership plus the iPhone cycle, modest XOM/CVX adds), since cash passively drags ~0.11% per 5 days vs SPY's +0.34% forecast and costs are only 10 bps each way. The retained 17% cash is an explicit buffer for the unmodeled week to the 10-02 cutoff (quarter-end, Q3 earnings start, LLY's binary 9/30 readout) and offsets the concentrated ~23% energy supply-shock bet the critic flagged; LLY and NVDA stay at 3% each — held for positive pre-event drift but not added, and V/JPM are left near current weights to avoid cosmetic churn.

forecaster.method_notes: Statistical drift-based forecasts over the actual 5-trading-day holding horizon (2026-09-25 to 2026-10-02), using only price history up to the decision date; one forecast per ticker, no lookahead. Benchmark SPY is expected +0.32% (p10 -1.97, p90 +2.68), so rank names by excess return vs SPY, not by sign vs zero. Largest positive excess: CAT +0.93, LLY +0.58, JNJ +0.55, XOM +0.43, AAPL +0.39, GOOGL +0.29, CVX +0.26; largest negative excess: HD -0.97, AMT -0.50, TLT -0.48, SO/SHW -0.46, PG -0.40, META -0.35. Limitations: (1) 5-day expected returns are tiny relative to the p10-p90 bands, so every directional call is low-conviction; wide intervals are uncertainty, not evidence an asset should be avoided. (2) The model is pure price-statistics drift and does not incorporate news, fundamentals, or event risk despite news being available. (3) Short-horizon drift can reverse: AAPL (RSI 74.6) and META (RSI 77.8) are extended, while NEE (16.4), SO (19.5), HD (25.9), and TLT (27.6) are oversold and prone to mean-reversion bounces the drift model may understate. (4) CAT's top excess return rests on 12-1 momentum (+76.5%) that conflicts with its live 90-day downtrend (-17.5%), echoing the stale-momentum concern flagged in the previous decision; its band is also among the widest. (5) Confidence is a subjective probability that the stated direction realizes, derived from the expected-return-to-interval-width ratio; all values sit near 0.5, honestly reflecting 5-day noise.
